description:
WHAT IT IS MADE OF. Every token is built from one primitive repeated hundreds of times: a flat, hard-edged rectangular bar or plank -- long thin slats, short stubs, and occasional near-square blocks -- laid down at many angles and many lengths, semi-transparent so that where bars cross they accumulate into brighter mass. There are no curves anywhere, no outlines, no text, no gradient fills; every mark is a straight-sided quadrilateral. Some seeds also carry a second, much finer primitive: hairline needles/threads a pixel or two wide (1475115, 1733538, 1835793, 1561509) that radiate from the core like whiskers. The ground is a near-black slate, not pure black, and it shows plainly at the corners of most frames.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. A frost crystal. Each token is a radial, roughly six-fold rosette -- a snowflake or an ice star -- assembled out of rectangular slats instead of dendrites. The reading is unmistakable and consistent: bright cream/ivory mass concentrated at the centre, arms of slats radiating out to the frame edge, hexagonal geometry recurring in the voids and in the silhouette. The 512 single reinforces it: a bright ice-white core with six arms of overlapping planks pushing outward through cooler blue-grey slats, like scaffolding seen through frost, or a shattered window read at the moment of the shatter. Secondary readings I kept coming back to: a mandala/rose window, a pile of milled lumber shot from above, pick-up-sticks.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Radial symmetry near six-fold; centre-weighted mass; the slat primitive; a two-family palette of warm ivory/bone against cool slate blue-grey on near-black; and the decision to let the composition run off all four edges rather than sit inside a margin. Every one of the twelve is centred, and every one of the twelve clips at the frame -- often with a bar terminating flush against the border (1203347 left edge, 1310661 bottom, 1985692 right).

HOW THEY DIFFER. Density and value are the main axes. 1446330 is the clear outlier: sparse, scattered, mostly dark ground, a thin spidery star with detached stubs floating loose -- it looks like the others exploded and drifted. 1561509 is the dark one: charcoal blocks, black ground dominant, a tight grainy core with pale needles, almost a negative of its siblings. 1366079 is the most graphic: a single solid ivory hexagonal plate at the centre, unbroken, with bars fanning off it. 1985692 and 1283437 invert the value relationship -- a heavy slate-blue lattice drawn ON TOP of a pale field, so they read as dark line-work over light, where most of the set reads as light mass over dark. 1310661 is the blobbiest: a nearly featureless white mass ringed by blue bars, with the least internal incident. The remaining group -- 1203347, 1243682, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793, 1991107 -- are close relatives: cream rosettes on black, separated mainly by how fine the tracery is and whether the centre is open (1203347 has a hollow hexagonal ring; 1243682 has a small dark hexagon; 1835793 and 1733538 have fine filigree cores).

WHAT HAPPENS ACROSS THE THREE STATES. The change is real and it is legible at 256. Broadly, NEUTRAL is the most resolved and open: 1203347's centre is a hollow hexagonal ring with visible tracery inside it, 1310661 is a clean bright disc, 1283437 balances pale field against grey lattice. STRESS consolidates and veils: 1203347's hollow centre fills in solid and the rosette stiffens into a blockier star; 1310661 gets crossed over by slate bars so the disc is scratched through; 1283437 darkens substantially, the cool slate taking over from the ivory; 1243682 swells and goes soft-edged and diffuse. RECOVERY is not simply a return to neutral -- it is a third thing. 1203347 recovers into the finest, most delicate state of the three, a dotted filigree core under long thin bars. 1243682 contracts, tightening smaller than neutral with a cleaner dark hex at the centre. 1283437 recovery is the DARKEST of its three frames, cooler and greyer than stress, which surprised me. 1310661 recovers its white core but keeps a heavy grey ring around it. So the axis being modulated seems to be density/consolidation and warm-to-cool value, not a simple damage-and-repair loop.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120. The silhouette survives completely -- at browse size every one of the twelve still reads as a frost rosette on black, and the six-fold geometry is still obvious. What does NOT survive is the fine tracery: the hairline needles in 1475115, 1733538 and 1835793 collapse into a soft cream haze, and the interior detail of 1203347's hexagonal ring becomes a grey smudge. The seeds that stay individual at 120 are 1366079 (solid disc centre), 1446330 (sparse and dark), 1561509 (dark and grainy), 1985692 and 1283437 (dark lattice over pale). The seeds that converge into one repeated stamp at 120 are 1203347, 1243682, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793 and 1991107 -- six of the twelve read as the same cream rosette with slightly different fringes. The state rows at 120 are distinguishable but require attention: neutral-to-stress is legible on all four (1283437 and 1310661 by value shift, 1203347 and 1243682 by the centre closing/opening), while stress-to-recovery is nearly invisible at that size on 1283437 and 1310661.

OTHER THINGS I NOTICED. The overexposure is a recurring condition rather than an accident: in 1203347, 1310661, 1366079 and 1991107 the accumulated alpha saturates to a flat ivory plateau with no internal information left, so the centre -- which is where the eye goes -- is the least informative region of the picture. There are stray isolated bars sitting alone in the black at frame corners on several seeds (1243682 upper-left, 1446330 throughout, 1985692 upper-right) which read either as deliberate scatter or as debris, and at 120 they read as dust on the lens. The clipping at the border is consistent enough across all twelve to be a decision rather than a bug.
